Field notes on slow travel

Slow travel is the practice of choosing fewer destinations and staying longer. It favours trains over planes, markets over monuments, and conversation over itineraries.

Travellers who adopt it report better sleep, lower spend per day, and a stronger sense of place. The trade-off is time: a week buys one region, not five countries.

Arrive late, leave early, and call it a plan.
